name: Dug wells in Neolithic Cyprus
summary: Early farmers on Cyprus had dug a well at Kissonerga-Mylouthkia by the time seeds fell into its fill, between 7500 and 6700 BCE.
description: At Kissonerga-Mylouthkia on Cyprus, a well (well 133) is assigned to the Cypro-Late Pre-Pottery Neolithic B. Two carbonised seeds from one of its fills gave a calibrated range of 7500-6700 cal BCE, which dates the filling and so gives the latest time by which the well had been dug. No other deposit in the well was dated, and the human remains found in it were not dated directly.

impact.note: Scored as the well-digging of one island's early farming communities (reach 1), though the source opened documents a single well; a water supply independent of streams and springs was a new capability (depth 2); no later well tradition is shown to descend from the Cypriot wells (generativity 0).

date.label: 7500-6700 cal BCE (fill of well 133)
date.basis: As the cited source gives it.

events.statement: Two carbonised seeds from one fill of well 133 at Kissonerga-Mylouthkia give a calibrated range of 7500 to 6700 BCE at 95% confidence; this dates the filling, so the well had been dug by then.

evidence.supports: The calibrated date range of these samples is 7500–6700 cal BCE
evidence.locator: Methods, archaeological context of the samples from well 133

earliest_record.rationale: The earliest dated evidence found for this capability in this community. No review has yet confirmed that nothing earlier exists.

unresolved.note: The source is a palaeogenomic paper that reports the well's date in passing; the Mylouthkia excavation report (Peltenburg and colleagues) should be opened for the older wells at the site, which are probably what the lead's c. 8500 BCE refers to.
Dates for Atlit Yam, Sha'ar Hagolan and Shillourokambos were not checked, so the earliest-well question and the Levantine half of the lead are open.
The date is from seeds in a fill, which gives a latest date for the digging of the well, not the date of digging.
Kissonerga coordinates were entered from memory and not taken from a fetched source.
The author list should be checked against the journal page.

research.note: The source opened does not say whether this was the earliest well anywhere, whether the Levantine wells named in the lead were earlier, or whether well-digging reached Cyprus with its settlers from the mainland.
